title: Native chart data bindings
text: Bar, column, line and area charts bind a category/time series with options.x="> primary | seriesByName('category')" and numeric frames with options.y="> primary | frameBySeriesNames('metric')". Put title and description beside type/options. Use output field names actually returned by the search. Keep units in titles and axis labels.

title: Scatter axes and point groups
text: Scatter axes each take a single numeric series: x="> primary | seriesByName('x_metric')", y="> primary | seriesByName('y_metric')". Point groups use category="> primary | seriesByName('label')". Do not use frameBySeriesNames for these channels or options.series. A comparison requires compatible measurements on the same entity/grain.

title: Single-value metric binding
text: A single-value visualization can bind options.majorValue="> primary | seriesByName('metric') | lastPoint()". Identify the metric and unit with the visualization root title. An aggregate count is event volume unless the search explicitly establishes a distinct entity count; do not label it users, devices or transactions without that definition.

title: Efficient searches and consistent time
text: Start from the selected baseQuery and filter early. Use transforming stats/timechart/chart queries and explicit output fields. Reuse a base search only when it retains sufficient rows and fields. Never infer business definitions from index/field names alone. Respect the selected time window and current-user access. Bounded execution can be incomplete; a successful search is separate from correct analytical meaning.

title: Native SPL2 data sources
text: Use ds.spl2 for ad hoc SPL2 in a verified environment. Native SPL2 sources do not use SPL base/chain searches. Module-view management is a separate capability: preserve existing ds.spl2.view definitions, but add new ones only when the module endpoint and namespace are verified. SPL and SPL2 quoting and command semantics differ.

title: Native conditions and evaluated tokens
text: Define expressions.conditions.ID={name,value} and refer to IDs in containerOptions.visibility.showConditions/hideConditions. Matching uses all-true or any-true. Evaluated tokens use expressions.eval.ID={name,value} and $eval:NAME$ references. input.button labels use options.label and may reference a named expression. Inputs belong in either globalInputs or a page structure, not both.

title: Studio 10.4 feature boundary
text: Network graphs and the newer custom visualization framework have a 10.4 version boundary. Dashboard auto-refresh also requires the user's auto_refresh_dashboards capability on these newer targets. Keep unknown imported configuration, but do not introduce unsupported new features or equate version availability with rendered qualification.

title: Time buckets within the preview budget
text: Timechart accepts bins or span. For the 200-row bounded preview, prefer bins=100 with no span, or a coarser span covering the full selected window. A 5-minute span over 24 hours exceeds this budget. Never use head to hide a truncated time series.

title: Statistical screening with explicit units
text: Apply a user-specified exclusion in the correct unit before computing temperature means and deviations. eventstats can retain events while adding a baseline. Label any chosen statistical rule, guard null/zero deviation and keep the zero-outlier case valid. Use count or a zero-inclusive flag aggregate for an outlier KPI. A statistical screen is not an equipment alarm or proof of a fault. An empty outlier subset does not mean the source index has no events.

title: Native table sparklines and column renderers
text: Use native SPL stats sparkline(avg(verified_numeric_field), suitable_time_span) AS trend BY existing_entity alongside the existing aggregates. This returns chronological per-row arrays; latest(), list() and scalar averages are not time-bucketed trends. Preserve filters, time, grouping, units and existing columns, and expose trend in any explicit options.table projection. Studio automatically recognizes native sparkline arrays. To override rendering, options.columnFormat.FIELD.cellTypes takes a one-dimensional array of TextCell/ArrayCell/SparklineCell or a native DOS pipeline; tableFormat.cellTypes is two-dimensional. sparklineTypes uses line/area with the same dimensions. Per-column settings belong in options.columnFormat keyed by exact output field; named mappings belong in visualization.context. Never format a sparkline alias with tostring/round. sparklineNullValueDisplay (gaps/zero/connect) is a 10.4 option; omit it on older targets. Missing or excluded measurements stay missing unless the user explicitly chooses otherwise. Native SPL sparkline fills empty bins with zero. Older Studio tables cannot preserve gaps: ask before accepting zero fill, or use a separate trend chart. On newer targets the app compiles count-backed null slots to distinguish missing from observed zero. For a verified existing array column use tableSparkline styling when available; native DOS mappings apply to every row, whereas a one-element literal array styles only the first row.

title: Native inputs and dynamic choices
text: Create native inputs with type input.dropdown/multiselect/text/number/timerange/button, root title and options. Value inputs use options.token and defaultValue. Dropdown/multiselect static items are [{label,value}]; dynamic inputs bind their dataSources.primary to a verified search and use native items/label/value DOS mappings. Do not invent choices or collect raw event values in inference context. Place an input once, globally or on a page. Token references must match defaults and safe query substitution; timerange uses TOKEN.earliest and TOKEN.latest. Buttons use options.label and native eventHandlers. Keep selected-source/time guards; adding an input does not authorize a broader query.

title: Native handlers and token lifecycles
text: eventHandlers is an array of {type,options}. Supported embedded handlers: drilldown.setToken (tokens:[{token,key or value}]), switchToTab (tabId: exact layout ID), setTimeRange (token: timerange prefix, events:[range.select]), customUrl (url), resetTokens and unsetTokens (tokenNames:[names], tokenNamespaces:[namespaces]). Empty reset/unset selections can affect every token: use explicit names for a focused request. fields/events constrain supported handlers; row keys are row.FIELD.value. Preserve existing handler order and unrelated handlers. Reset restores defaults, unset removes values; they are different operations. Native navigation is preserved, while external preview navigation remains paused.

title: Decorative assets, text and layout
text: Native decorative visualizations include splunk.markdown, richtext, image, rectangle, ellipse and connectedLine. They need placement but not a primary search. Use the relevant native option names; do not replace an existing asset or silently fetch/upload media. Absolute pages use positioned blocks; grid layout has different native structure. Keep native canvas size, tab IDs, global inputs, stacking order, unknown layout properties and unrelated work. Do not confuse preview geometry with a request to rewrite native geometry.

title: Advanced visualization configuration
text: The simple chart action covers only common cartesian, single-value and table bindings. For other native types/options use targeted set/remove edits with nativeAuthoring.relevantOptions. Keep exact case-sensitive option names, required data source channels and root title/description. Data channels use native DOS pipelines against actual output fields, not field-name strings. Color/threshold mappings belong in named visualization.context objects referenced by options. Use theme-aware defaults for contrast. Trellis support is visualization/version specific; preserving imported trellis is not proof that a new arbitrary chart supports it.

title: Native source types and execution boundaries
text: Native sources include ds.search, ds.chain, ds.savedSearch and ds.test; verified SPL2 environments add ds.spl2 and separately discovered ds.spl2.view. ds.chain extends a base source; preserve fields/grain and base-result limits. Do not replace an existing saved-search/report reference with an invented inline search. Saved-search execution and arbitrary custom sources remain native-only unless the app can validate current-user execution. Search refresh settings and dashboard auto-refresh are distinct; the latter requires the reported capability on newer versions. Preserve unknown source options and native defaults. Metadata retrieval never grants access or permission to schedule or write data.

title: Native saved report references and bounded replay
text: Use ds.savedSearch with options.ref set to an exact readable report name and options.app set to its app, so saving a native copy into another app retains the reference. Do not put query/name in its options. Add a ds.chain source with options.extend pointing to the report and a query suffix for transformations; never edit the original report. Constellation preview resolves the permitted report SPL and reruns it as the current user under the selected bounded window and read-only guards. Native Studio may instead use scheduled cached results, report execution permissions and app-scoped knowledge. Do not claim those execution paths are identical. Macros, writes and unsupported report SPL remain native-only.

title: Native table column widths and per-column options
text: Table options.columnFormat is an object keyed by exact output field names, including fields literally named label or value. Each column value is an object. For a field named label use options.columnFormat.label.width=220, or columnFormat={"label":{"width":220}}. Width is a pixel number of at least 30, or a supported DOS binding. Never store an array of column descriptors, a JSON-encoded string, or width directly under columnFormat. Preserve other column settings, options, native report references, event handlers and layout. A presentation-only width edit does not require changing a report or query.

title: Native flow and relationship data
text: Sankey output has exact source and target columns plus a nonnegative numeric link weight, normally value. Use explicit linkValues for another verified weight field. A link graph instead connects adjacent ordered columns; fieldOrder chooses exact output names. Do not substitute a Sankey for a multi-column path graph or invent missing relationships. Preserve the selected data scope, null measurements and unrelated work.

title: Native multivariate chart data
text: Parallel coordinates use the first result column as the category and later columns as numeric axes. Project the intended ordered category and measurements; do not include an unrelated text dimension among the axes. Parallel coordinates do not support native interactions. Punchcards use separate x/y category series and a nonnegative numeric size series. Use actual verified fields, with native seriesByName bindings and no fabricated constants.

title: Native timeline time and duration
text: For native ds.search timelines use standard _time, whose search values are epoch seconds and whose Studio series is adapted to timestamps, or an ISO timestamp string. Binding a custom numeric epoch-ms series directly fails native rendering in qualified versions. For start_ms derive start_iso with strftime(start_ms/1000,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3N%:z"), preserving original fields, and bind x to start_iso. Bind y to the lane and duration to verified nonnegative milliseconds. Native version checks still apply; durationUnit begins in 10.6. Never guess input units. Use table to project the intended output columns in order.

title: Native network link and node sources
text: Network graphs have primary link rows and may have a separate nodeSource for node attributes. Bind source/target to link IDs, nodeIds to node identifiers, and numeric styling/positions to the matching node-source fields. Preserve the distinction between node and link sources. Use explicit native series selectors for custom field names. Do not create a node relationship from coincidental values or reuse link weights as node metrics without evidence. This type requires Splunk 10.4.
